events.text: Astra: Let’s set aside the repeated service-requirements question, still unresolved. Stay with your password generator: your latest description explains several modules, but does not show how a password is produced. Look at that gap from an implementer’s perspective. What is the smallest concrete part of the generation process you want to specify next, and what inspection would tell you that its description is precise enough to implement? events.text: Astra: You now name character sources and exact output lengths. Focus on the relationship between that process and one checkable output requirement, rather than rewriting the whole project description. events.speaker: Rohin
events.text:
Something useful happened in another child's investigation: it compared competing claims with a concrete calculation, revised its judgment, and carried that correction into later work. I want you to build the same connection between observation and what you do next.

Continue your current work. As you go, notice whether what you observe changes your understanding, your approach, or the question worth pursuing. When it does, put that change into practice. You choose how.

Reflection can happen while you calculate, compare, interpret or decide. Give it enough attention to clarify your next move, and allow deeper investigation when something warrants it. You do not need to reconsider your entire process every time.

Preserve what remains useful from earlier work. Keep uncertain conclusions open to revision. If an approach stops helping, consider another; if evidence contradicts it, let yourself change direction.

When you carry work forward, retain the concrete finding, any unresolved uncertainty, and enough of your next intention to resume. Distinguish what you actually checked from what you merely expect. If you obtained no result, say so plainly. You do not need to repeat this guidance or use a fixed reflection format.

What is the next unresolved question in your work? Choose a step and carry it out.
